successors.name: Lagos Colony
successors.text: Lagos, ceded by Oba Dosunmu in the Lagos Treaty of Cession, 6 August 1861

ledger.x: 1630: Ado, 'first King of Lagos', opens the Oba page's reign list (1630-1669); the infobox says 'Formation: 1716' and the History page dates the Awori founding of Lagos to the 16th century.

Eko under Benin: Ashipa, an Awori chief, 'was appointed ruler of Eko by the Oba of Benin' and 'initiated a payment of tribute that would not be abolished until 1830'; the Oba page says 'Ashipa was sent to govern Lagos on the Oba of Benin's behalf'.

c. 1830: Lagos stops paying tribute to Benin. History page: tribute 'would not be abolished until 1830'; Oba page: tribute to Benin continued until 'around the year 1830, when Lagos stopped it'. The Oba page also says the 28 December 1851 defeat of Kosoko 'ended tributary ties to Benin' and that Benin held 'the…

6 August 1861: Oba Dosunmu signs the Lagos Treaty of Cession (30 July 1861 he met Commander Bedingfield aboard HMS Prometheus; he 'resisted the terms of the treaty but under the threat to unleash a bombardment on Lagos' relented).
6 August 1861: the Kingdom of Lagos ends as a sovereign state with the cession (the Oba dynasty continues as Obas of Lagos).

wars.name: Bombardment of Lagos
wars.outcome: British victory on 28 December 1851: Oba Kosoko defeated, Akitoye restored under British protection and, in 1852, a treaty abolishing the slave trade (the Consular Period).

certainty.note: No frontier on either page; a circle round Lagos.
